specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins: a friendly cartoon photograph of a smiling cat that is gently lifting up one corner of itself like a curtain, revealing that underneath the picture is actually a neat grid of little numbered squares (a grid of cells each holding a small number), as if the photo and the spreadsheet of numbers are one and the same thing. A small friendly robot stands beside it pointing back and forth between the photo side and the grid side with a delighted expression. The style should be friendly and approachable, like a comic strip or an XKCD-inspired infographic, with expressive characters and minimal visual clutter, suitable for a technical textbook. Use only a few tiny incidental numbers in the grid; no sentences, no labels, no lettering or words anywhere. The humor is gentle: the picture is literally made of numbers. Keep the composition simple and focused on one clear visual metaphor.
specs.alt: A cartoon cat photograph peels back its own corner to reveal it is secretly a grid of numbers underneath, while a friendly robot points between the photo and the number grid, illustrating that in Python an image is not represented by an array, it literally is a NumPy array of pixel values.
specs.caption: An image in Python is not represented by an array; it is one, and every NumPy trick you know already works on pictures.

specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins: a friendly cartoon brightness dial or odometer-style gauge that only goes up to a maximum tick mark, with a little robot enthusiastically cranking a lever to add more brightness. The needle has shot past the maximum and wrapped all the way back around to the very bottom near zero, so the scene that should be getting brighter has instead gone dark; a small sun icon that was glowing is now dim and surprised. The robot looks baffled, scratching its head. The style should be friendly and approachable like an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive characters, minimal clutter, suitable for a technical textbook. No text, no numbers on the dial, no lettering or words anywhere. Gentle humor: trying to brighten something made it darker. Keep the composition simple and focused on one clear visual metaphor.
specs.alt: A robot cranks a brightness dial past its maximum tick and the needle wraps around to the bottom, turning a bright sun dim, illustrating how uint8 pixel values overflow modulo 256 so that adding brightness can paradoxically make pixels darker.
specs.caption: Push an 8-bit pixel past 255 and it does not stop at the ceiling; it wraps around to the floor, so adding light can leave you in the dark.

One is a sturdy industrial worker in a hard hat (the fast workhorse), one is a tidy scientist in a lab coat holding a magnifying glass (the careful scientist), one is an elderly distinguished librarian or archivist holding a file folder (the file-format elder), plus a couple more small helper figures. specs.alt: A glowing NumPy array cube sits at the center as a friendly host while a worker in a hard hat, a scientist with a magnifying glass, an elderly archivist, and other specialist characters all speak to it through empty speech bubbles, illustrating that OpenCV, scikit-image, Pillow and the rest are not rivals but dialects of one shared array language.
specs.caption: The imaging libraries are not competitors; they are specialists who all speak to the same NumPy array, each in its own dialect.

specs.anchorText: It is the digital equivalent of photocopying a photocopy
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins: a friendly cartoon photocopier in the center with a line of paper copies coming out of it in a row, left to right. The first sheet shows a crisp clear smiley sun, the next is slightly fuzzier, the next blockier and speckled, and the last one on the right is badly degraded, blocky and smudged into a sad blur, while a small worried robot holds up the worst copy and compares it to the crisp original. Each successive copy is visibly worse than the one before. The style should be friendly and approachable like an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive characters, minimal clutter, suitable for a technical textbook. No text, no numbers, no lettering or words anywhere. Gentle humor: nobody noticed any single copy looked bad, yet the last one is a mess. Keep the composition simple and focused on the progressive-degradation metaphor.
specs.alt: A photocopier emits a row of copies of a smiling sun that get progressively fuzzier and blockier from left to right while a worried robot compares the worst copy to the crisp original, illustrating how repeatedly re-saving a JPEG compounds compression loss like photocopying a photocopy.
specs.caption: Lossy compression is a one-way door: each re-save quietly degrades the picture, and the tenth copy is plainly worse than the first even though no single save looked destructive.

specs.anchorText: Same bytes, two meanings: red in one world, blue in the other
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins: in the center sits one identical sealed envelope or parcel (representing a fixed triplet of bytes). Two friendly cartoon characters stand on either side reading the very same parcel, but each holds a different colored pair of glasses. The character on the left, wearing glasses that tint things one way, sees and reacts to a bright red heart floating above the parcel and smiles. The character on the right, wearing differently tinted glasses, reads the exact same parcel but sees a blue heart instead and looks puzzled. A subtle equals-style visual link shows the parcel is identical for both. The style should be friendly and approachable like an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive characters, minimal clutter, suitable for a technical textbook. No text, no numbers, no lettering or words anywhere. Gentle humor: same thing, two opposite readings. Keep the composition simple and symmetric, focused on one clear metaphor.
specs.alt: Two cartoon characters read the same identical sealed parcel through differently tinted glasses, one seeing a red heart and the other a blue heart, illustrating that the byte triplet 255,0,0 means red under RGB and blue under OpenCV's BGR convention because the array itself never records which channel order it follows.
specs.caption: The very same bytes mean red in the RGB world and blue in OpenCV's BGR world; the array never records which convention it follows, so only your code knows the truth.

specs.anchorText: every vision system in this book, however sophisticated, has the same skeleton
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins: a friendly cartoon conveyor-belt assembly line running left to right with five distinct little stations, each staffed by a small cheerful robot doing one job. At the first station an image arrives (a small framed picture), at the second a robot inspects it with a checklist clipboard and a magnifying glass, at the third a robot reshapes or polishes the picture, at the fourth a robot holds up a measuring gauge or ruler against it, and at the fifth a robot files the finished picture into a labeled storage box. The five stations are clearly sequential along the belt. The style should be friendly and approachable like a Kurzgesagt-meets-XKCD infographic, expressive characters, minimal clutter, suitable for a technical textbook. No text, no numbers, no station labels, no lettering or words anywhere. Keep the composition simple, a clean left-to-right assembly line of five steps.
specs.alt: A cheerful five-station conveyor belt where small robots in turn receive an image, inspect it with a checklist, transform it, measure it with a gauge, and file it into storage, illustrating the load, validate, transform, measure, save skeleton shared by every vision system in the book.
specs.caption: Load, validate, transform, measure, save: every vision system in this book is these same five stations, and the two beginners always skip are the inspector and the one with the ruler.
